name: Gold Coast Quarry
summary: In southwestern Westfall, the Gold Coast Quarry has fallen to the Defias Brotherhood. The mine once supplied Stormwind with stone, minerals, and gold; now the Brotherhood draws on its remaining resources for its insurrection.

sections.title: A Plundered Resource
sections.body: The Gold Coast Quarry once supplied Stormwind with stone and gold for the kingdom's rebuilding. After royal troops withdrew from Westfall, Defias highwaymen and renegade laborers seized the mine. Brotherhood patrols watch from its terraced ramps, which overlook the coast, and take what minerals remain to fund their rebellion.

faq.q: What was the quarry originally used for?
aliases: why is there a quarry here
faq.answer: The Kingdom of Stormwind opened the quarry for stone, minerals, and gold. Stone taken from quarries across Westfall helped support Stormwind's reconstruction after the Second War.

faq.q: Who controls the Gold Coast Quarry right now?
faq.answer: The Defias Brotherhood controls the quarry. Its brigands, looters, and highwaymen patrol the terraced cliffs and mine entrances, keeping settlers away as they extract resources for their own operations.

faq.q: Why hasn't Stormwind sent guards to clear the quarry?
faq.answer: With King Varian Wrynn missing, the Stormwind House of Nobles is unwilling to fund a standing garrison in Westfall. The crown has abandoned the region, leaving the People's Militia to fight for control of places like the quarry on their own.

faq.q: Where is the Gold Coast Quarry located?
aliases: how to find gold coast quarry
faq.answer: The Gold Coast Quarry cuts into the cliffs of southwestern Westfall, south of the Saldean and Alexston farmsteads, overlooking the Great Sea.

angles.text: As a miner in Westfall, you can find rich stone faces and mineral veins along the quarry cliffs. Working them means fighting through entrenched Defias patrols.
As an Alliance member, reclaiming sites like the Gold Coast Quarry is vital to restoring order in Westfall. With no royal garrisons, local volunteers have taken up arms.
